title: Linear-simulator sequential indifferentiability from an ideal cipher
summary: Construct an ideal-primitive block cipher whose sequential ideal-cipher simulator uses only linear queries and incurs essentially linear-over-domain distinguishing error.

formal_statement.body: Construct a block cipher from a fixed ideal primitive, together with a simulator, that is sequentially indifferentiable from an ideal cipher with simulator-query complexity $\sigma=O(q)$ and distinguishing error $\varepsilon=O(q/2^n)$ for a $q$-query distinguisher, or prove the target impossible for the stated ideal-primitive domain.

scope.domain: Ideal-primitive block-cipher constructions under sequential indifferentiability from an ideal cipher.
assumptions: The construction uses a source-defined ideal primitive such as a random oracle or a fixed finite tuple of public random permutations.
The distinguisher follows the source sequential query order.
Simulator cost is measured in queries to the ideal cipher.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Known IEM constructions reduce the round count and attain polynomial simulator costs, including $O(q^2)$ with an $O(q^4/2^n)$-scale error, but the simultaneous $O(q)$ and $O(q/2^n)$ targets remain open.

progress.summary: A five-round non-idealized-key-schedule IEM is proved indifferentiable, but with substantially larger polynomial simulator and error losses.
A four-round two-permutation construction attains sequential indifferentiability with $O(q^2)$ simulator complexity and an $O(q^4/2^n)$-scale error.
